chapters.title: Levers of Influence: Power Tools of the Trades
chapters.sourcePressure: Automatic compliance can be triggered by a single cue, as in fixed-action patterns, click-run responding, weak because-reasons, trigger features, and contrast effects.
chapters.coreMove: Spot the trigger feature before you treat the yes as your own full judgment.
chapters.commonMisread: Persuasion is just people being irrational or gullible.

chapters.title: Reciprocation: The Old Give and Take
chapters.sourcePressure: Favors, gifts, free samples, uninvited debts, unequal exchanges, concessions, and rejection-then-retreat can make repayment feel compulsory.
chapters.coreMove: Pause after a gift or concession and decide whether you received generosity or an obligation device.
chapters.commonMisread: Always repay kindness quickly to stay honorable.

chapters.title: Liking: The Friendly Thief
chapters.sourcePressure: Attractiveness, similarity, praise, cooperation, association, and friendly selling can transfer good feeling onto a request.
chapters.coreMove: Separate warmth toward the messenger from the merits of the decision.
chapters.commonMisread: Good relationships are dangerous or friendliness is fake.

chapters.title: Social Proof: Truths Are Us
chapters.sourcePressure: Popularity cues, uncertainty, similarity, pluralistic ignorance, staged audiences, and descriptive norm messages can make others' behavior look like evidence.
chapters.coreMove: Ask whether the crowd signal is real, relevant, and made of people comparable to you.

chapters.title: Authority: Directed Deference
chapters.sourcePressure: Rank, expertise, legitimacy, titles, uniforms, and status cues can direct deference before relevance is checked.
chapters.coreMove: Verify whether the authority signal is genuine and qualified for this exact choice.

chapters.title: Scarcity: The Rule of the Few
chapters.sourcePressure: Limited availability, threatened loss, closing access, fewness, and urgency can make value feel larger than it is.
chapters.coreMove: Remove the loss pressure long enough to price the option by its use, not its disappearance.
chapters.commonMisread: Rare things are always better or urgency is always manipulation.
mustNotDriftInto: fear of missing out as lifestyle talk

chapters.title: Commitment and Consistency: Hobgoblins of the Mind
chapters.sourcePressure: Prior choices, public stands, visible commitments, identity alignment, and lock-in can pressure people to keep obeying old decisions.
chapters.coreMove: Treat consistency as evidence to inspect, not a command to continue.
chapters.commonMisread: Consistency is bad and changing your mind is always brave.

chapters.title: Unity: The We Is the Shared Me
chapters.sourcePressure: Shared identity, belonging, we-ness, common fate, and boundary softening can make another person's interest feel like part of the self.
chapters.coreMove: Distinguish real shared identity from borrowed belonging cues before letting scrutiny drop.
chapters.commonMisread: Unity is just liking, similarity, or rapport.

chapters.title: Instant Influence: Primitive Consent for an Automatic Age
chapters.sourcePressure: The closing synthesis gathers the levers into a system of fast-trigger consent under modern cue saturation without re-teaching each lever.
chapters.coreMove: Recover a deliberate inspection pause when several cues make agreement feel pre-approved.
chapters.commonMisread: The ending is just a recap of seven principles.
